summary: Volume variances at meters (nominated vs metered vs allocated vs counterparty-reported) are found late, by hand: in the UA4 report, in month-end imbalance reviews, or when a counterparty calls asking to be paid. Each one is then worked through email chains to Daren Farmer that sit for days. A daily variance job would compare actuals against nominations, POPS allocations and Sitara deals, then send each flagged meter to its owner with the deal and contract history already attached. That replaces the research-and-chase emails, and the estimated value is $91 per month ($1,092 per year) at $85 per hour.

current_workflow.step: A scheduler or volume analyst spots a variance at a meter: a counterparty short on nomination, a meter receiving under nom, or an interconnect not pulling gas. They email the volumes by day and ask the logistics desk how to handle it.
Accounting or storage desks compare counterparty or confirmed volumes against what was booked, attach spreadsheets, and ask for the best way to correct the difference.

Unallocated volume shows up on the UA4 report. The analyst searches OSS and CPR for a deal, then reconstructs the meter's contract history month by month to work out which contract should take the volume.
When POPS feeds zero or stale volumes to Sitara, someone spots the imbalance later and asks for a manual override of POPS daily volumes using flow data from Gas Control, so the P&L is right.
current_workflow.who: risk / imbalance reviewer and volume management

current_workflow.step: The issue goes to the logistics lead (Daren Farmer) or a trader for a decision on deal setup, buyback, reallocation or wellhead purchase. Requesters follow up with status emails while it waits.

Items that are still open are gathered into periodic outstanding-issue lists with deadlines, for example for the intercompany cleanup before SAP implementation. Unresolved ones show up as payment disputes from counterparties.

There wasn't any deal in

stall_points.description: Unresolved allocation turns into counterparty payment demands handled by phone, because nobody caught the gap before settlement.
stall_points.quote:
I am getting several phone calls from Alpine Resources demanding to be paid 
for meter 5892 and there is nothing there to be paid.

solution.approach: A daily variance job reads meter actuals (Gas Control and HPL Measurement daily flow) and compares them, by meter and day, with confirmed nominations and POPS allocated volumes and with the volumes on the Sitara deals tied to each meter. It flags four cases: (a) flow with no deal or no allocatable contract, which would otherwise land in UA4; (b) POPS volume of zero or missing while the meter shows flow, which is the stuck-feed case; (c) a gap between actual and nomination above a set tolerance, for example short or under-nom days; and (d) two desks using different measurement sources at one meter. For every flagged meter it builds a case sheet showing the meter's contract and deal history by month, so the analyst no longer has to reconstruct it from OSS and CPR. Each case goes to the meter's assigned volume analyst, and anything needing a commercial call goes to the logistics lead in a single daily digest instead of separate emails. Open cases age on a shared list that replaces the hand-built outstanding-issues email, so follow-up nudges are automatic.
solution.trigger: Daily schedule after Gas Control / measurement actuals are loaded, plus a month-end run before the UA4 report is finalized
inputs: Daily meter actuals from Gas Control / HPL Measurement
Confirmed nominations by meter and day
POPS allocated daily volumes and meter allocation settings
Sitara deal numbers and volumes per meter
Deal and contract history in OSS and CPR per meter
Tolerance thresholds per meter or counterparty
outputs: Daily variance list by meter and day with variance type, for volume management analysts
Case sheet per flagged meter with contract and deal history, so no manual research is needed
Daily decision digest for the logistics lead (Daren Farmer) listing meters needing a buyback, deal setup or reallocation call
Shared open-issues list with age and owner, replacing the periodic outstanding-issues email
Month-end UA4 pre-check showing volumes still lacking a contract before close
components: Daily meter variance comparison job with configurable tolerances
Meter contract-history lookup that builds the case sheet
Routing table mapping meters to responsible analysts
Daily decision digest email for the logistics lead
Shared open-variance tracker with owner, age and resolution code

implementation_steps: Confirm with volume management and Gas Control which extracts exist for daily actuals, confirmed nominations, POPS allocations and Sitara deal volumes, and agree on one meter-day key.
Build read-only extracts and a variance comparison script covering the four flag types (no deal, zero POPS feed, nomination gap, source mismatch).
Set tolerances with the logistics lead, starting wide to avoid noise, and keep the meter-to-analyst assignment list.
Add the contract-history lookup from OSS and CPR so each flagged meter gets a month-by-month case sheet.
Run in shadow mode for one month next to the current process and compare the flags with the variance emails that actually came in, then tune the tolerances.
Turn on routing, the daily decision digest and the shared open-issues tracker; retire the hand-built outstanding-issues list.
Add the month-end UA4 pre-close run, and review open-case age weekly with the volume management lead.
stays_manual: Deciding whether to set up a deal, arrange a buyback, reallocate, or treat gas as a wellhead purchase. These are commercial calls for the trader or logistics lead.
Entering POPS overrides and reallocations. A person confirms the Gas Control figures before changing allocation that feeds the P&L.
Settling disputes with counterparties and interstate pipelines (for example over who has custody transfer or which measurement is authoritative), which needs negotiation and sometimes Legal.
Researching historical meters whose assignment changed and where records are incomplete. The case sheet helps, but someone still has to judge which contract should have been used.
risks: The evidence does not show what form the actuals, nomination and POPS data come in or whether automated extracts exist. If they don't, the effort could grow from M to L, so confirm data access first.
Tolerances set too tight will flood analysts with noise and the alerts will get ignored. Mitigate with shadow mode and per-meter thresholds.

Different measurement sources (for example pipeline volume vs HPL Measurement) can produce false variances. Record which source is authoritative for each meter and flag disagreements as their own case type.
Preliminary flow data can change after it is first reported. Re-run on revised actuals and mark cases as provisional until measurement is final.
The dollar value is modest ($91 per month) because it covers only email handling time. Avoided P&L hits from volumes sitting in UA4 are real but not quantified here.
success_metric: Number of meter-days with flow but no deal or zero POPS volume still open at month-end UA4, and median days from variance to resolution
